title: Who's Who: Adelaide Wren
summary: Expedition engineer whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Adelaide Wren (1809–1876) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a expedition engineer whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Wren built the restraint and recovery mechanism for the 1844 tethered brass probe. She insisted that the first probe carry no inscription that might bias its return, then spent years disputing claims that its pale mineral deposit had been planted.
The anchor point of that departure became the Prime Referent of later surveys.

For Alderwick readers, Adelaide Wren is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
